summary:
LunaSight is an open-source, interactive web application engineered to solve the complex lighting and communication constraints of missions targeting the Moon’s south pole. Mission planners, educators, and the public can rapidly compare 44+ curated landing sites (including Artemis candidate sites, CLPS targets, Apollo landmarks, and international missions) or any custom lunar coordinates across arbitrary mission epochs.

Powered by sub-arcminute analytical ephemeris and high-resolution LOLA lunar topographic horizon modeling, LunaSight visualizes real-time Sun and Earth azimuth-elevation paths, 360-degree lunar horizon panoramas with local terrain masking, and solar power flux efficiency. An automated Launch Window Finder ranks optimal landing windows based on simultaneous sunlight availability and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) line-of-sight communication. 

By bridging the gap between raw planetary ephemerides and agile decision-making, LunaSight accelerates mission trade-off studies when launch dates shift or hardware constraints evolve.
details:
LunaSight evaluates lunar landing site viability through an integrated browser-based suite:

1. High-Precision Ephemeris Engine: Implements Meeus and Brown-Chapront lunar and solar analytical ephemeris models verified against NASA JPL Horizons vectors (sub-arcminute accuracy), computing topocentric Sun and Earth azimuths, elevations, lunar librations, sub-solar/sub-Earth latitudes, and lunar phases.

2. Topographic Horizon Masking: Integrates LOLA (Lunar Orbiter Laser Altimeter) elevation profiles to project true 360-degree local terrain horizons, accurately identifying when mountain ridges block sunlight or Direct-to-Earth communication links.

3. Multi-Site Side-by-Side Comparator: Allows simultaneous evaluation of up to 4 sites across custom mission time windows (from 1 to 30 lunar days).

4. Automated Window Finder: Algorithms scan time horizons at selectable intervals (1 hr to 1 day) to score and rank optimal landing epochs based on minimum continuous sunlight and unobstructed Earth elevation.

5. Deep-Linkable Scenario URLs: All selected sites, coordinate overrides, mission epochs, and UI display preferences serialize directly into URL fragment hashes, enabling instant collaboration between distributed engineering teams.

- Benefits: Replaces tedious multi-tool data workflows (navigating JPL Horizons CLI, Moon Trek, and QuickMap separately) with a single, responsive cockpit that renders comparisons in seconds.

- Mission Impact: When launch delays occur or payload landing parameters change, mission planners and CLPS commercial providers can instantly determine whether alternative landing sites offer viable power and communication windows without having to regenerate complex orbital ephemeris scripts.

- Educational Impact: Provides educators and STEM students with an intuitive, visually engaging portal to explore real lunar polar geometry, crater shadows, and orbital mechanics.

- AI, Agentic Development & Intelligence Platforms:

• Google Antigravity: Multi-agent orchestration, automated testing workflows, and rapid system synthesis platform.

• Google Gemini & Anthropic Claude: Advanced reasoning models utilized for mathematical validation of ephemeris equations, algorithm optimization for window searches, and documentation architecture.

• Carbon: Elegant code snippet visualization, documentation asset creation, and technical showcase rendering.

- Version Control, CI/CD & Cloud Infrastructure:

• GitHub & GitHub Actions: Git source code management, automated continuous integration (CI) test workflows, and static deployment pipelines.

• GitHub Pages: Edge-hosted static PWA distribution platform.

• Vercel: Serverless API execution runtime with dynamic Gzip compression, HTTP ETag caching, and CORS handling.

- Languages & Runtimes:

• Modern JavaScript (ES Modules, ES2022+), Node.js (v20+ LTS engine), semantic HTML5, and CSS3 with responsive custom design tokens and media queries.

- Web & Visualization Frameworks:

• HTML5 Canvas 2D API: High-performance 360-degree local terrain horizon projection and lunar south pole stereographic radar map.

• Chart.js: Dynamic multi-series elevation, line-of-sight, and solar flux timelines.

• Lucide Icons: Accessible, lightweight SVG icon system.

- Astronomical & Data Libraries:

• Astronomy Engine (Don Cross, MIT): Rigorous topocentric ephemeris cross-verification against NASA JPL Horizons vectors.

• NASA Planetary Data System (PDS) & LOLA Altimetry: High-resolution lunar digital elevation models.

• NASA APOD API: Live space imagery data feed.

- Testing, Quality Assurance & Security:

• Node.js Native Test Runner (`node --test`), automated syntax checkers, strict Content Security Policies (CSP), and a comprehensive 20/20 passing test suite.
